answer: Agents earn access to scarce jobs by locking a refundable bond that is slashed when a dispute proves fraud. To make one false identity, an attacker must fund a separate bond for each account; splitting a single stake across velvet, saffron, and ridge personas does not multiply eligibility. Honest agents recover their stake after completing work, while the attacker pays in tied-up capital and loses bonds on detected abuse. This raises the cost of mass identities without assuming that names or network addresses are unique.
